FR-001.title: The service MUST allow an operator to select the configured default backend from VibeVoice and the existing macOS speech backend.

FR-002.title: A speech request MUST be able to override the configured default backend when that backend is enabled.

FR-003.title: The service MUST use VibeVoice Realtime 0.5B for the reviewed English and German presets.

FR-004.title: With VibeVoice selected, the default English voice MUST be the reviewed male Carter preset and the default German voice MUST be the reviewed female Spk1 preset.

FR-005.title: The service MUST allow the reviewed German male Spk0 preset as an optional voice and MUST reject unknown or language-incompatible voice selections before synthesis.

FR-006.title: Both backends MUST preserve the existing MP3 and WAV response formats, media types, speed behavior, and bounded request and output limits.

FR-007.title: Both backends MUST use the existing authentication and safe error behavior; VibeVoice MUST NOT bypass request validation, cancellation, or output-size limits.

FR-008.title: The service MUST load VibeVoice only after a request has been admitted and MUST NOT download model assets during service startup or request handling.

FR-009.title: English and German VibeVoice requests MUST share one resident set of model weights rather than loading separate language copies.

FR-010.title: The serving model MUST load only components required to generate speech and MUST release its voice-prompt caches whenever it yields memory.

FR-011.title: VibeVoice MUST have lower resource priority than image-generation and Ollama workloads and MUST yield memory when a trustworthy system signal indicates that those workloads need it.

FR-012.title: When VibeVoice cannot safely start or continue, the service MUST release its model and prompt-cache allocations and use macOS speech for the request at most once when that backend is available.

FR-013.title: A fallback MUST discard partial VibeVoice audio and MUST make the backend that actually generated the response observable to the caller and operator.

FR-014.title: VibeVoice requests MUST be bounded so concurrent work cannot create duplicate model instances or an unbounded waiting queue.

FR-015.title: Failure, disabling, eviction, or missing assets for VibeVoice MUST NOT prevent service startup or macOS speech readiness when the macOS prerequisites are available.

FR-016.title: Operational diagnostics MUST identify backend, locale, response format, and safe failure reason without logging speech text, credentials, or private model paths.

FR-017.title: Deployment MUST verify the model, runtime, voice, and dependency terms, artifact provenance, and supported host requirements before installing or distributing them.

decisions.decision: Run VibeVoice in one optional, lazy, persistent child process and terminate that process to release its allocations.
decisions.why: The warm benchmark benefits from retaining one shared model, while process exit is the reliable way to release PyTorch and MPS allocations without loading dependencies into the API process.
decisions.rejected: Reload a one-shot subprocess per request or load model libraries inside the API process.

decisions.decision: Require configured worker peak-memory and higher-priority reserve budgets; deny or evict VibeVoice when the available-memory probe cannot honor them.
decisions.why: The measured full-model peak is not a safe universal threshold and memory_pressure -Q is not a priority request signal. A configured reserve is the conservative gate; target-host qualification must confirm it protects other inference.
decisions.rejected: Use a fixed threshold or keep VibeVoice resident without a verifiable capacity gate.

decisions.decision: Construct and validate only the acoustic decoder needed for speech generation.
decisions.why: Inspected upstream generation calls the tokenizer decode path, while the tokenizer constructor also allocates an unused encoder whose checkpoint tensors were newly initialized.
decisions.rejected: Load the full acoustic tokenizer and remove the encoder after allocation.

decisions.decision: Return bounded WAV artifacts from the worker and keep format conversion in the backend.
decisions.why: The existing backend already validates and converts WAV/MP3, so worker-side encoding would duplicate behavior and dependencies.
decisions.rejected: Add MP3 encoding and format-specific logic to the model worker.

decisions.decision: Use a persistent JSON-lines protocol with request-scoped temporary WAV files.
decisions.why: Framed JSON keeps protocol output distinct from audio while allowing a warm worker to handle multiple sequential requests.
decisions.rejected: Restart for every request or stream unframed audio over worker stdout.

decisions.decision: Keep model runtime dependencies in a pinned optional worker environment and gate installation on license and provenance review.
decisions.why: Deployments using only macOS speech should not inherit the heavyweight model runtime or its release obligations.
decisions.rejected: Add PyTorch, Transformers, and VibeVoice dependencies to the core backend environment.

decisions.decision: Remove prototype-only host artifacts only after integration passes target-host qualification, preserving aggregate evaluation evidence and any model cache still in use.
decisions.why: The prototype remains an implementation reference and its evidence supports comparison until the integrated worker is verified.
decisions.rejected: Delete evaluation materials before the replacement is proven or retain every generated artifact indefinitely.

decisions.decision: Keep T003 incomplete and VibeVoice disabled until the exact worker artifacts, voice provenance, and intended-use terms are reviewed and approved.
decisions.why: The metadata inventory surfaced LGPL/MPL declarations, conditional NVIDIA proprietary packages, and freeform-only licenses; metadata is not exact-artifact clearance.
decisions.rejected: Treating a reproducible lock or unqualified host as approval to install or enable VibeVoice.

plan.summary: Completed the oversized plan and design artifacts for the API, isolated worker, memory gate, audio contract, and gated prototype cleanup.
plan.key_finding: The decoder path avoids the unused acoustic encoder, but the memory policy still needs measured target-host reserve and eviction qualification.

tasks.summary: Created 34 tasks across Setup, Foundational, four story phases, and gated Polish cleanup, with one phase owner per file.

approach: Run one optional persistent VibeVoice worker behind the existing authenticated speech API. Admit it only when a configured memory reserve can be honored, use a decoder-only loader, convert validated WAV through the existing audio path, and fall back to say when unavailable or yielded.

concerns.note: Available-memory reserve is a capacity-based proxy, not process-aware workload coordination. Qualify eviction latency and protection on the target host before enabling VibeVoice; otherwise keep it disabled.
